title: Do toads cause warts?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore whether toads cause warts (they do not; warts are caused by the human papillomavirus, HPV, and toad 'warts' are actually glands). The episode covers the giant cane toad's introduction to Australia to control cane beetles, its spread and toxins, HPV and its strains including the mandatory vaccination push (Women in Government and Merck), how common warts spread and resolve, treatments like cryotherapy and salicylic acid, blister beetle extract, and an old wives' tale about burying a dead cat. The episode also includes a blog and spoken-word album plug for the Stuff You Should Know Super Stuff Guide to the Economy, and listener mail from Alex in Germany and a fan named Martin.
topics: Super Stuff Guide to the Economy

segments.title: Opening banter and warts memories
segments.summary: The hosts open the show, discuss their personal experiences with warts (plantar warts, burning them off with liquid nitrogen), and the common claim that toads cause warts.

segments.title: Giant cane toads in Australia
segments.summary: Australia imported 101 giant cane toads from Hawaii in the 1930s to control cane beetles in sugar cane fields; the toads did not control the beetles and have multiplied into billions, spreading toward cities. Their toxins kill predators such as crocodiles and dingoes. The hosts mention the documentary Cane Toads: An Unnatural History.

segments.title: Toads do not cause warts
segments.summary: Warts on toads are glands, not warts. Toads cannot give humans warts because warts are caused by HPV, which toads do not carry.

segments.title: HPV and the vaccination debate
segments.summary: HPV affects many people and has about 100 types; some cause cervical cancer and others genital warts. The hosts discuss the 2006-2007 push for mandatory HPV vaccination for girls, the role of Women in Government and its funding from Merck, the only maker of an FDA-approved HPV vaccine, and state legislation.

segments.title: How warts spread and treatments
segments.summary: Common warts are not cancerous, spread by contact and shared objects, and eventually go away as the body fights them, though they can spread as they shed. Treatments include cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen, over-the-counter salicylic acid, laser surgery, and prescription drugs for genital warts. Blister beetle extract also causes blistering. A folk remedy of burying a dead cat at midnight is dismissed.

segments.title: Blog and spoken-word album plug
segments.summary: Hosts plug the Stuff You Should Know blog and the spoken-word album The Stuff You Should Know Super Stuff Guide to the Economy, available on iTunes.
